To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Instagram is a useful data source to study food and drinks consumption patterns, and that these patterns are consistent with the official statistics.

(a) Instagram posts can provide a rich source of data to study food & drink consumption in everyday-life; (b) the food & drink consumption of the Swiss population is characterized by a high diversity of food & drink items, with a high consumption of coffee and chocolate and a high diversity of breakfasts; (c) the food & drinks consumption is highly concentrated in the evening and at the weekend, with the exception of coffee, which is mostly consumed during the morning;

(a) Instagram data can be analyzed to extract food & drink consumption and eating event patterns, and (b) these patterns are consistent with official statistics and with previous research on food and drink consumption, (c) supervised machine learning models can discriminate eating events based on their content, context and social features, and (d) healthy eating posts are more likely to be liked and shared than unhealthy eating posts, and (e) the most popular food and drink items are those related to coffee and tea
In summary, our research is concerned with

(a) the study of food and drink items and consumption patterns in social media, (b) the analysis of the eating event classification problem using social media data, and (c) the comparison of social media insights with official statistics.
the analysis and prediction of food & drink patterns in social media, with a focus on healthy eating events.
the extraction of food and drink patterns from Instagram posts, and with the use of these patterns for supervised learning of eating event classes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
social media are a rich source of data for the study of food and drink in daily life.

Instagram posts can be used to extract meaningful patterns of food and drink consumptions, but that supervised learning tasks are still limited by the lack of a large and diverse set of labelled examples.
social media data are useful in understanding food consumption patterns and can be leveraged to infer food and drink consumption events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

social media provide a rich data source for studying food and drink consumption, and that the combination of content and contextual features are promising for the automatic classification of food and drink items.
social media can help to better understand food consumption and eating events in everyday life.

the social media can be used as an alternative source to study food consumption in everyday life, and that the analysis of the data can be used as a basis for the definition of tasks for supervised learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the analysis of social media data can provide a new perspective to study food consumption patterns, and that the classification of eating events from social media data is a promising approach for the study of eating behavior.
social media data can be used to study and infer food & drink consumption in everyday-life.

the analysis of food and drink posts on social media can provide a complementary perspective to official food and drink consumption statistics, with the potential of improving the accuracy and granularity of the latter.
